$comment: APPROVED, NAMED, EXPIRING suppressions for the integration shard.
A test that appears here is still counted against the full EXPECTED population. It is not removed
from the denominator, because reducing the denominator by the tests you expect to skip encodes the
suppression into the success criterion: the gate then passes forever while those tests never run.
Every suppression this project has found was justified when it was written, and every one survived
for the same structural reason -- doing nothing preserved it. So neglect must REMOVE a suppression,
* expires, id and owner are MANDATORY. An entry missing any of them fails the gate, so the
* a PAST expiry is a REFUSE, not a warning. The suppression stops working and the build stops.
* renewal requires FRESH EVIDENCE, not a fresh date. Bumping the date is the failure mode that
would defeat the whole mechanism, because it makes an unreviewed entry LOOK reviewed. Record a
new measurement in evidence: what was run, on what, and what it showed.
* the list may only SHRINK. Growth is a reviewable diff with a named approver, never a runtime
The gate prints this file in full on every run, with days remaining. Suppressions become invisible
by going unread; this is the one moment someone is looking.

REFERENCE DIRECTION. This file is world-visible, so it carries NO internal tracker id. The tracking issue names this entry by its 'id'; this entry never names the issue. Internal artifacts may point at public ones, never the reverse -- a public file that cites an internal work item leaks it and means nothing to the consumer reading it.

entries.reason: Eleven external-vault facts call SkipIfVaultUnavailable(), which skips when AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI is unset. Four argument-validation facts in the same class execute without a vault and are not covered by this budget. The external tests need a real Key Vault resource and credentials in the CI environment.
entries.evidence: RENEWED 2026-10-31 on a NEW measurement, after the 2026-10-30 expiry REFUSED all six integration legs. Run: the class alone, Release, --no-build, AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI deliberately unset to reproduce the CI condition. Result: 15 total, 4 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed. All 11 skipped names were enumerated individually and every one belongs to this class and reports 'AZURE_KEYVAULT_URI environment variable not set'; the 4 that passed are the argument-validation facts. Source re-derivation the same day independently agrees: 15 [Fact] members, 11 of which invoke the availability guard, 4 of which do not. PRIOR EVIDENCE, kept because it is still the stronger whole-shard figure: measured 2026-10-23 in a Release Dispatch integration run, 2061 passed, 11 skipped, 0 failed, with adapter discovery and per-name TRX accounting agreeing on 2072 total. Passing the four argument-validation facts does not establish that the external-vault facts pass against Azure; that coverage remains UNVERIFIED and requires a configured test vault. THE REMEDY IS TO DELETE THIS ENTRY, NOT TO RENEW IT AGAIN. These eleven are skipped because they are written to require a live vault, and no Key Vault emulator exists; a dated budget can only postpone that. The first-party answer is two-tier and neither tier is a skip: replay a recorded, sanitised HTTP session on every build so the provider's request/response contract is covered deterministically with no credentials, and run the genuinely live suite on a separate schedule against provisioned resources. The replay tier is buildable here without recording infrastructure, because the client accepts a transport and a stubbed one returns canned responses. Whoever reads this next should convert the eleven to the replay tier and remove this entry; the live tier needs a funded vault and credentials, which is an owner's decision, not a test-authoring one.

entries.reason: Every arm skips because the Elasticsearch container was not reachable from InitializeAsync. Unlike the sibling Azure Blob suite, whose skip turned out to be an API-version rejection by a running container, this one appears to be genuine absence.
entries.evidence: Measured 2026-08-02 on the CI integration shard. The skip reports '[infrastructure-unavailable] Elasticsearch (Docker) was not reachable from InitializeAsync'. Corroborated independently by the coverage artifact from the SAME run: MonitoredResilientElasticsearchClient is 0.0% covered, 0 of 614 lines, across all four result files -- so no arm executed anywhere in the shard, not merely in this class. The contrast is the point: Azure Blob's cold store read 85.0% covered while its own suite skipped, which is how that skip was exposed as a false claim of absence. RENEWED 2026-10-02, and one of the two open questions is now CLOSED: all 8 arms PASS against a reachable Elasticsearch, 0 skipped, measured locally on Docker in 5 seconds. So the arms are sound and the skip is purely about reachability in CI's environment. STILL NOT established: WHY the container is unreachable there. This renewal is deliberately short because the remaining question is a CI-environment defect that an allowlist cannot fix, only postpone.
